title: Keeping promises small and kept
description: The secret to a reputation for reliability is not bigger promises — it is smaller ones, fully kept.

body.heading: Shrink the promise to the certain
paragraphs: Generosity makes promises swell: “I’ll read the whole draft and send detailed notes by Friday.” Reality then edits them. The reliable learn to promise the version they can do on their worst week — “I’ll read the first chapter by Friday” — and then, often, delight by delivering more.
A promise kept at exactly its size is worth more than a larger one kept approximately. People plan around your words; accuracy is kindness.

body.heading: Renegotiate before you break
paragraphs: Sometimes even the small promise becomes impossible. The move that saves trust is early honesty: “Friday has collapsed — can I get it to you Monday?” said on Wednesday. The same message sent on Saturday is not a renegotiation; it is a confession.
Almost everyone forgives an early renegotiation. Almost no one forgets being silently stood up by a promise.

body.heading: Keep a promises list
paragraphs: It sounds mechanical and works like magic: one list, somewhere you actually look, of everything you have told anyone you would do. Most broken promises are not betrayals; they are paperwork failures. Fix the paperwork and your character gets the credit.
Reliability, it turns out, is mostly a filing system plus the will to shrink your yes to a size your calendar can carry.

takeaway: Promise the certain version, renegotiate early when life intervenes, and keep one honest list.
